To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cyclic variations in methane-fueled spark-ignition engines are mainly due to variations in the relative location of local eddies with the spark plug, which in turn is due to the random distribution of the local eddy length and the random location of the spark plug in the engine cylinder.
the cyclic variability of a spark-ignition engine can be determined accurately by simulating only five representative cycles.
a fast CFD-based methodology has been developed for estimating the cyclic variability in SI engines.

the development of fast CFD-based methodologies for determining cyclic variability in SI engines.
the development of a fast methodology for estimating the cyclic variability in SI engines and its effects on engine performance and emissions.

the proposed methodology can be used as a fast tool for the estimation of cyclic variability, and its effect on performance and emissions, in SI engines.

a fast methodology for determining cyclic variability and its effect on performance and emissions of SI engines has been developed and validated for methane-fueled engines, and that it is now ready for future applications.

a fast CFD-based methodology for determining the COV of the IMEP and its effects on the performance and pollutant emissions of spark-ignition engines is now available.
